assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental and theoretical analysis of reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion changed the economic account of behavior and has durable influence across labor, organizational, and public economics.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt supplied a central formal framework, while Fehr and Falk were leading contributors to the experimental evidence and its economic applications.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work is longstanding, extensively tested in diverse settings, and has generated a mature research program.
uncertainties: The breadth of the literature makes the boundary between foundational contributors and later extensions difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioral game theory made laboratory evidence a central tool for testing economic institutions and strategic behavior.
assessment.attribution: Plott, Holt, and Camerer each made foundational but complementary contributions to market experiments, experimental methods, and behavioral strategic reasoning.
assessment.maturity: The empirical tradition is decades old, widely replicated, and embedded throughout modern economics.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping spans several related contributions and omits other important pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of present bias, self-control, and reference-dependent preferences supplied influential alternatives to time-consistent expected-utility accounts and reshaped work on saving and policy.
assessment.attribution: Laibson, O'Donoghue, and Rabin have clear foundational roles in formalizing behavioral departures with tractable economic implications.
assessment.maturity: These ideas have had long-run theoretical and empirical influence, including substantial experimental and field evidence.
uncertainties: The broad grouping combines distinct preference mechanisms.
The appropriate allocation of credit among the listed scholars is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established a compelling account of how technology, tasks, and trade shocks reshape local labor markets and wage inequality, with unusually broad public and scholarly consequence.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are closely identified with the decisive empirical and conceptual advances on these linked labor-market changes.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been repeatedly examined over more than a decade and have prompted a large subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The causal magnitude and generality of particular trade-shock effects remain actively debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification fundamentally clarified what data can and cannot establish under credible weak assumptions, improving the honesty and usefulness of empirical inference.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the unmistakable central architect of the underlying intellectual program; the other listed contributors advanced important related methods.
assessment.maturity: The framework is longstanding, technically mature, and influential across econometrics and applied work.
uncertainties: Its more specialized practical uptake may be less visible than that of some broader empirical programs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions and skill formation convincingly redirected attention toward the long-run economic consequences of childhood health and investment.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond developed influential empirical evidence on early-life shocks, while Cunha made major contributions to the dynamic theory of skill formation.
assessment.maturity: The program has accumulated extensive evidence, policy relevance, and a durable interdisciplinary literature.
uncertainties: The candidate combines empirical early-life research with a broader structural theory, making a single prize citation less compact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design provided a powerful general framework for analyzing strategic disclosure and the design of information environments.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Bergemann originated the core persuasion framework, while Morris made foundational contributions to the wider theory of information in strategic settings.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical program is highly influential and has spread rapidly into many economic applications.
uncertainties: Its relatively recent emergence and evolving empirical application leave its ultimate durability less certain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary accounts of routines and organizational capabilities offered a lasting alternative lens on firms, innovation, and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is a foundational and readily identifiable contributor to this intellectual tradition.
assessment.maturity: The work has had decades of influence across organizational and evolutionary economics.
uncertainties: The contribution is intertwined with collaborators and a broad intellectual lineage not fully represented by this single-name candidate.
